# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 25 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 25 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**25:1** [...] for [...] my heart [...] has trembled at Your judgments [...]

**25:2** [...] and my reins are dissolved, and my bones are shattered [...]

**25:3** [...] and my heart pours-out like water, and my flesh melts like wax [...]

**25:4** [...] and my knees give-way like water poured-out on a slope [...]

**25:5** [...] and I said: In my transgression I am abandoned [...]

**25:6** [...] from Your covenant. But when I remembered the-strength-of Your hand [...]

**25:7** [...] together with the-abundance-of Your mercies, I stood-upright and rose [...]

**25:8** [...] and my spirit held-fast to its station, for I leaned [...]

**25:9** [...] upon Your lovingkindness, and the-abundance-of Your mercies [...]

**25:10** [...] for You atone for transgression, and You purify a man from guilt by Your righteousness [...]

**25:11** [...] and [...] my strength [...] has failed before Your glory [...]

**25:12** [...] and there is no remnant, and no strength [...] in me [...]

**25:13** [...] I am struck-dumb, for what shall I speak that is not known [...]

**25:14** [...] and what shall I declare that is not told? All things [...]

**25:15** [...] are engraved before You with the-stylus-of remembrance for-all the-appointed-times [...]

**25:16** [...] of eternity, and the-seasons-of the-number-of everlasting years [...]

**25:17** [...] in all their appointed-times, and they shall not be hidden [...]

**25:18** [...] from before You. How shall a man recount his transgression? [...]

**25:19** [...] and how shall he plead concerning his iniquity? [...]

**25:20** [...] and how shall he reply to righteous judgment? [...]

**25:21** [...] To You, O God-of knowledge, belong all the-works-of righteousness [...]

**25:22** [...] and the-counsel-of truth; but to the-sons-of man belongs the-service-of iniquity [...]

**25:23** [...] and the-works-of deceit. You have created breath for the-tongue [...]

**25:24** [...] and You know its words, and You established the-fruit-of the-lips [...]

**25:25** [...] before they existed. And You set words upon a line [...]

**25:26** [...] and the-utterance-of the-breath-of the-lips by measure [...]

**25:27** [...] and You bring-forth sounds according-to their mysteries [...]

**25:28** [...] and the-outpourings-of breath according-to their reckoning, to make-known [...]

**25:29** [...] Your glory and to recount Your wonders [...]

**25:30** [...] but Your mercies [...] have sustained me in all these things [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 25 is very fragmentary. The surviving text captures a powerful lament: physical collapse (trembling, melting, failing strength) followed by recovery through divine mercy. The language of physical dissolution (25:1-4) is characteristic of the Hodayot's somatic theology. The stylus-of-remembrance imagery (25:15) reflects the predestinarian worldview. Construct chains preserved throughout.*
